key_insight: A specially shaped capillary cavity can passively eject centimeter-scale liquid drops that relax faster into near-spherical form during short microgravity windows.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical design rules for drop-tower and microgravity droplet generators that must produce usable drops within only a few seconds.
method: Optimized parabolic cavity geometry for a fixed liquid volume to minimize initial surface area.
Used smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations to compare relaxation times after capillary auto-ejection.
Tested a modified cavity with a shallow central depression to further speed relaxation.
evidence_signal: Simulation results showed the surface-area-minimizing parabolic cavity also gave the shortest relaxation time in its family, while a central depression reduced relaxation time even further.
watch_item: The best-performing cavity introduces geometric complexity and may be sensitive to fabrication tolerances, liquid properties, and microgravity operating conditions.
paper_title: Rapid generation of relaxed centimeter-sized drops by capillary auto-ejection
